context:
The repair input uses the built-in 'edges' fixture. Its original cue records, in this exact processing order, are:
- id 'first', start_ms -2000, end_ms -100, text 'Before.'
- id 'touch', start_ms -100, end_ms 0, text 'At zero.'
- id 'cross', start_ms -50, end_ms 300, text 'Across zero.'
- id 'unicode', start_ms 300, end_ms 900, text 'こんにちは — hello!'
- id 'out', start_ms 10000, end_ms 14000, text 'Beyond.'
- id 'late', start_ms 100, end_ms 200, text 'Out of order.'

All times are integer milliseconds. The candidate timings supplied with the run already add offset_ms to both endpoints, clip endpoints to [0, duration_ms], and — after any previously retained cue — raise a start (never an end) to at least that previous retained cue's end_ms plus gap_ms, without re-clipping the raised start. Retain a candidate exactly when its start_ms < end_ms; otherwise drop it. A dropped cue does not update the previous retained end, the first retained cue has no leading-gap requirement, and do not sort: keep retained cues and dropped IDs in original order. Copy each retained cue's id, start_ms, end_ms and text unchanged (the 'unicode' text includes Japanese characters and an em dash). Use [] for an empty list. Copy the run and task values exactly as supplied.
